turns.t: Good morning, doctor. I hope this isn't too trivial. My ears feel blocked, ever since I flew back from Boston on Friday.
Not trivial at all. Tell me what the blocked feeling is like.
Like I'm underwater. Muffled, and a sort of fullness, mostly in the right ear.
When did it begin, exactly?
On the descent. They popped in the first ear, but the right one never did, and it's been four days now.
Any pain in the ear? ~
A dull ache on the descent, but nothing since. Just the muffled feeling. ~
Does it crackle or pop when you swallow?
Occasionally, a little crackle. Then it goes quiet again.
Have you tried anything to clear it? ~
I tried holding my nose and blowing gently, a few times. I read it online. ~
That's a good method, as long as it's gentle. Let me look in your ear. ~
Of course.
The right eardrum is slightly pulled in, but it's intact and there's no fluid or infection that I can see.
Is it serious? ~
Not at all. It's a common thing after flying, when the tube that equalises pressure behind the eardrum is slow to open. ~
Will it clear by itself? ~
Almost always, within a week or two. ~
Is there anything I should do? ~
Chew gum or suck a sweet, yawn, and do that gentle blowing with your nose pinched, a few times a day.
I can do that. ~
Steam from a hot shower or a bowl of hot water also helps. ~
I'll do that tonight. ~
And don't fly again for now if you can avoid it, and don't put anything in the ear.
Understood. What if it doesn't clear? ~
If it's not better in two weeks, or you get pain, discharge or dizziness, come back and see me.
I will. Thank you so much. ~
You're welcome. Safe travels, whenever you next go. ~
Thank you, doctor. I'll chew plenty of gum. ~
Please do. ~
